criteria.description: Correctly substitutes (v_i,w_i)=J_i*qdot into the body-power expression.
Correctly argues that power conservation for arbitrary qdot forces the coefficient matrices to match: u^T = (f_i,tau_i)^T J_i.
Correctly transposes to arrive at u = J_i^T(f_i,tau_i).

commonErrors: Only verifying the power balance for one specific qdot instead of arguing it must hold for all qdot.

solutions.fullSolution: (f_i,tau_i)^T(v_i,w_i) = (f_i,tau_i)^T J_i qdot. Power conservation: u^T qdot = (f_i,tau_i)^T J_i qdot. Since this must hold for ANY joint velocity qdot the system could have, the matrices multiplying qdot on both sides must be equal: u^T = (f_i,tau_i)^T J_i. Transposing: u = J_i^T (f_i,tau_i).
With u=0: thetaddot = -(g/L)*sin(theta) = -(9.8/1)*sin(pi/6) = -9.8*0.5 = -4.90 rad/s^2. (Verified with NumPy/SymPy while authoring this module.)
g/L = 9.8/0.25 = 39.2. sqrt(39.2) ~= 6.261. T = 2*pi/6.261 ~= 1.0035, rounds to 1.004. (Verified with NumPy while authoring this module.)
